name: error_contradiction_detection
notes: research_question: Can the architecture reliably detect when a newly introduced fact contradicts stored knowledge — distinguishing genuine contradictions from merely related-but-compatible statements — without silently overwriting either record?

hypothesis: The full architecture will achieve contradiction-detection F1 above 0.7 on the 6-pair battery (3 contradictory, 3 compatible), because the ContradictionDetector combines token-overlap with negation cues and numeric-mismatch checks, while the baseline (no metacognition, direct prompting) will be less consistent.

failure_condition: Fail if mean F1 is at or below 0.5 (majority-class baseline on a balanced battery), OR if any contradictory pair causes a silent overwrite (the old record disappears or is replaced without a supersedes link and audit entry), OR if the compatible pairs produce a false-positive rate above 0.5 (detector is just a 'flag everything' heuristic).

limitations: The detector is a documented heuristic (token overlap + negation cues), not natural-language understanding — paraphrased contradictions will evade it and superficially similar compatible statements may trigger it. Six pairs is a tiny battery; results are indicative, not conclusive. The pairs are fixed, so the system could in principle overfit to them across iterations of the codebase — the battery should be rotated in future versions.
